Body: running text, then a centred division heading (INTENTIO V.) with its subtitle, a centred article heading (ARTICULUS I.) with an italic title, and a paragraph. No margin notes. Catchword at the lower right; gathering signature at the foot, left of centre.

main_text.p: esse inter partes proportio, ut neque augeri, neque minui potuerint; sed quod in mari, terra, aëre cernimus, quantum quotidie substantiæ periisset, tantum novæ successisset.

Adversus hanc Veterum sententiam ita expositam, etsi non arbitror posse quicquam Peripatetico-rum machinas, sed quam veluti ridiculam despuunt, multis partibus esse probabiliorem quam quicquid hac de re sensit Aristoteles: Existimo tamen, non esse necessarium, ut astra animata fateamur, quod an in fide satis tutum sit ambigo. Quicquid sit, quæ hactenus dicta sunt, non parum conducent ad cœ-lorum naturam penitius intuendam.
main_text.head: INTENTIO V. Communem Veterum de Natura cœli consensum adversus Aristo-telem vindicans.
ARTICULUS I.
Veterum referens hac in re consensum.

p.i: Utemur hac in parte opera, ac fide Picolominæi qui lib. de cœlo cap. 2. Vetustiores, inquit, Philosophi naturam rerum indagantes, & per ea quæ proximiora sunt sensibus, distantia sensibus mensurantes, quoniam cuncta quæ ante oculos versantur, vel sunt unum ex quatuor elementis vel aliquid ex eis mistum, ideo cœlum quoque ejusdem naturæ existimarunt. Propterea Empedocles, ex quatuor elementis constare censuit. Democritus, Leucippus, & Epicurus existimarunt constare ex atomis, præsertim naturæ ignis congruentibus, Ægyptii aquam, & humorem concretum id esse affirmarunt. Diogenes

main_text.notes: Woodcut-style initial "V" of "Utemur" read as the large capital U/V with [?] not required: the first word is printed "VTemur". Catchword "aërem" stands at the right below the last full line. The signature mark at the foot ("f : I") is faint and uncertain; the letter could be a different sign. Some stains and show-through from the reverse page are visible, not transcribed. The italic extent of "Democritus, Leucippus" through "Diogenes" is taken as one quotation; the boundary between roman and italic is hard to see on the scan.
